executiveSummary: Available reporting indicates a confirmed cyberattack against CEVA Logistics, a CMA CGM subsidiary, disrupting multiple European warehouses and creating credible maritime supply-chain and customer-impact risk. View Article U.S. MARAD Advisory 2026-007 warns that foreign-manufactured port equipment and logistics platforms (including LOGINK, Nuctech scanners, and remotely serviceable ship-to-shore cranes) may enable adversarial data access and remote manipulation across maritime IT/OT, recommending immediate segmentation, MFA, monitoring, PLC integrity checks, offline backups, and restricted vendor remote access. Government Advisory Threat environment: Current reporting suggests moderate risk driven by an active third-party logistics compromise and ongoing systemic port OT concerns. Confidence: medium. Active incidents: CEVA disruption is likely to produce knock-on delays, partner portal access issues, and increased fraud/phishing attempts targeting maritime customers and suppliers. Source Critical advisories: MARAD's guidance remains highly relevant for port and terminal operators, especially where remote maintenance and logistics data aggregation are in use. Government Advisory Navigation/communications: No confirmed GPS/GNSS/AIS/ECDIS disruption or SATCOM degradations were reported in this collection window. Operational and safety implications: The collected intelligence supports an assessment that third-party logistics compromises may impede cargo movement planning and EDI/document workflows, while port OT exposure could-if exploited-affect crane operations or terminal throughput. Confidence: medium. Immediate attention: Validate third-party dependencies (warehousing, 3PLs), restrict remote vendor access into port OT, verify offline backups and PLC baselines, and heighten monitoring for partner-originated phishing or fraudulent routing instructions. Recommendations reflect reported guidance and standard defensive practices. Government Advisory
